item.title: Water Heater Not Heating? What to Check First
item.description: For an electric water heater, check the breaker first, then press the red high-limit reset behind the upper access panel with the power off. For gas, confirm the gas valve is open and the pilot is lit, following the lighting label on the tank. If a reset trips again or the pilot will not stay lit, call a licensed pro.

item.title: Refrigerator Not Cooling? What to Check
item.description: Check that the temperature controls are set correctly and the cooling is not switched off or in demo mode, make sure vents inside are not blocked by food, check the door seals, and clean dusty condenser coils with the fridge unplugged. If those checks do not help, a fan, compressor or control likely needs a technician.

item.title: How to Winterize Outdoor Faucets and Prevent Frozen Pipes
item.description: Before the first hard freeze, disconnect and drain hoses, close the indoor shutoff valve for each outdoor faucet, then open the outdoor faucet to drain and leave it open. Add an insulated faucet cover. Keep the house heated to at least 55 degrees F when you are away.

item.title: How to Weatherstrip an Exterior Door
item.description: Close the door on a sheet of paper or look for daylight to find gaps, then replace worn weatherstripping on the jamb with a matching compression or kerf-in seal and add or adjust a door sweep at the bottom. The door should close with light resistance and no daylight showing.

item.title: How to Unclog a Toilet
item.description: Use a flange plunger with a tight seal and pull back as hard as you push, about a dozen strokes. If plunging fails, a closet auger (toilet auger) clears most stubborn clogs without scratching the bowl.

item.title: How to Unclog a Sink Drain Without Chemicals
item.description: Start by pulling and cleaning the stopper, then plunge with the overflow blocked. If that fails, clean the P-trap under the sink or run a hand drain snake. Skip chemical drain cleaners; they rarely clear a full clog.

item.title: How to Stop a Smoke Alarm From Chirping
item.description: A single chirp every 30 to 60 seconds usually means a low battery: replace it with the type printed on the alarm and press TEST. If it keeps chirping with a new battery, or the alarm is 10 years past its manufacture date, replace the whole alarm.

item.title: How to Reset a Tripped GFCI Outlet
item.description: Unplug everything on the dead outlets, find the GFCI outlet with TEST and RESET buttons (it may be in another room, the garage, or outside), and press RESET firmly until it clicks. If it will not reset or trips again right away, leave it off and call an electrician.

item.title: How to Reset a Tripped Circuit Breaker
item.description: Turn off or unplug what was running on the dead circuit, open the panel, and find the breaker sitting in the middle or off position. Push it fully to OFF, then back to ON. If it trips again right away or keeps tripping, stop and call an electrician.

item.title: How to Replace an Electrical Outlet
item.description: Turn off the breaker, prove the outlet is dead at both receptacles with a tester, photograph the wiring, and move each wire to the matching terminal on a new outlet of the same rating: black to brass, white to silver, bare to green. Stop and call an electrician if the wiring is different or damaged.

item.title: How to Replace a Window Screen
item.description: Pop out the old rubber spline, lay new screen mesh over the frame, and press it into the channel with a spline roller and new spline, working around the frame while keeping the mesh taut. Trim the excess with a utility knife.

item.title: How to Replace a Light Switch
item.description: Turn off the breaker, confirm the power is off with a voltage tester, take a photo of the wiring, then move each wire to the same terminal on an identical new switch and connect the ground. If the wiring does not match what you expect, stop and call a licensed electrician.

item.title: How to Regrout Tile
item.description: Scrape out the damaged grout with a grout saw or oscillating tool to about 1/8 inch deep, vacuum and dampen the joints, press new grout in diagonally with a rubber float, wipe the haze with a damp sponge, and let it cure before caulking corners or sealing.

item.title: How to Recaulk a Bathtub or Shower
item.description: Remove all the old caulk, clean off residue and mildew, let the joint dry completely, then tape both sides, run a bead of kitchen and bath caulk, smooth it, pull the tape while wet, and let it cure for about 24 hours before using the tub.

item.title: How to Patch a Small Hole in Drywall
item.description: Fill nail holes and dents with spackling or joint compound in two or three thin coats, sanding lightly between. For holes from about 1 1/2 to 6 inches, cover the hole with a self-adhesive metal or mesh patch first, then feather three thin coats of compound over it, prime and paint.

item.title: How to Patch a Large Hole in Drywall
item.description: Cut the damage into a clean square, screw wood backing strips inside the opening, screw in a matching piece of drywall, then tape the seams and finish with three thin coats of joint compound before priming and painting.

item.title: How to Fix a Squeaky Door Hinge
item.description: Tighten the hinge screws first, then tap out each hinge pin one at a time, clean it, and coat it with a light multipurpose oil or a dry graphite lubricant before tapping it back in. If a screw spins without tightening, fill the hole with glued wood slivers and redrive it.

item.title: How to Fix a Running Toilet
item.description: A toilet that keeps running is almost always leaking past a worn flapper or overfilling through the overflow tube. Do a food-coloring dye test, adjust the chain or float, and replace the flapper or fill valve if adjusting does not stop it.

item.title: How to Fix a Leaky Outdoor Faucet (Hose Bib)
item.description: If water leaks around the handle, tighten the packing nut behind the handle a quarter turn. If the spout drips with the handle closed, shut off the water to the spigot, unscrew the stem, and replace the rubber washer on the end. A spigot that leaks inside the wall after a freeze needs a pro.

item.title: How to Fix a Leaky Faucet
item.description: A dripping faucet usually has a worn cartridge, washer or O-ring. Shut off the water under the sink, remove the handle, pull the old cartridge or washer, and install an exact match from the faucet's manufacturer.

item.title: How to Fix a Leak Under the Sink (P-Trap and Drain)
item.description: Dry everything, run water, and watch to find the exact drip. Leaks at the curved P-trap are usually fixed by reseating or replacing the slip-nut washers or swapping in a new plastic trap kit; leaks at the supply lines need a new braided connector.

item.title: How to Fix a Jammed Garbage Disposal
item.description: Turn the disposal switch off (unplug it or shut the breaker if you can), insert the 1/4 inch hex wrench into the socket in the center of the bottom of the unit, and work it back and forth until it turns freely. Remove the loosened object with tongs, let the motor cool, press the red reset button on the bottom, and test with cold water running.

item.title: How to Fix a Door That Won't Latch
item.description: Find where the latch hits the strike plate (a little lipstick or chalk on the latch shows it), tighten the hinge screws, then file the strike opening a little larger or move the strike plate to line up. A longer screw in the top or bottom hinge can raise or lower the door.

item.title: How to Fix a Door That Sticks
item.description: Find where the door rubs, then tighten the hinge screws, especially the top hinge; a longer screw into the framing often pulls a sagging door back square. Only if that fails, plane or sand the tight edge and seal the bare wood with primer and paint.

item.title: How to Fix Low Water Pressure at a Faucet (Clean the Aerator)
item.description: If only one faucet has weak or sputtering flow, the aerator screen at the tip of the spout is probably clogged with sediment or mineral scale. Unscrew it, rinse and soak it in white vinegar, or replace it with a new aerator of the same size.

item.title: How to Fix Drywall Nail Pops
item.description: Press the drywall tight to the stud and drive a drywall screw about 1 1/2 inches above and below the popped nail, then set or remove the nail and cover everything with two or three thin coats of compound. Covering the pop alone will not last.

item.title: How to Find and Shut Off Your Main Water Valve
item.description: The main shutoff is usually where the water line enters the house: in a basement or crawl space on the front wall, near the water heater, in a garage, or in a utility closet. Turn a round gate valve clockwise until it stops; turn a ball valve lever a quarter turn so it sits crosswise to the pipe.

item.title: How to Clean a Dryer Vent
item.description: Unplug the dryer (and shut off gas at the dryer's valve for a gas dryer), pull it out, disconnect the duct, and run a dryer vent brush through the duct and the wall vent to the outdoor hood. Vacuum the lint trap housing, reconnect with rigid or semi-rigid metal duct, and check that the outside flap opens when the dryer runs.

item.title: How to Clean Gutters Safely
item.description: Set an extension ladder on firm, level ground with a stabilizer so it rests on the roof rather than the gutter, scoop debris into a bucket starting near the downspouts, then flush the gutters and downspouts with a garden hose. Clean at least twice a year, more often under trees.

item.title: Dishwasher Not Draining? How to Fix It
item.description: Check the sink side first: run the garbage disposal, clean the air gap cap if you have one, and look for a kinked drain hose. Then pull and rinse the filter in the bottom of the tub. On a newly installed dishwasher, the disposal's knockout plug may still be in place.

item.title: Little Giant recalls about 3.66 million ladders with Rapid Locks over fall hazard
item.description: The CPSC and Little Giant announced a recall of about 3.66 million ladders with Rapid Locks because they can suddenly retract if the locks are not fully engaged. Owners should stop using them and contact Little Giant for a repair kit.

item.title: DREO recalls about 338,800 DR-HSH015 ceramic space heaters for fire risk
item.description: DREO recalled about 338,800 DR-HSH015 ceramic space heaters made from April 2025 through January 2026 because they can overheat and ignite. Stop using them and contact DREO for a free replacement.

item.title: CPSC warns two sets of combination smoke and CO alarms sold online fail to alarm
item.description: The CPSC told consumers to stop using JuzhiAnn, Yfwsrecinoe and JAEHSKA alarms (model JZA-540COM) and GuardianSense/KLTseanife alarms (model YHW-542COM-R) because they fail to sound in the presence of smoke and fire. The sellers have not agreed to recalls.

item.title: CPSC warns PowRyte electric pressure washers lack GFCI protection at the plug
item.description: The CPSC warned consumers to stop using PowRyte pressure washers sold on Amazon and eBay because they lack a ground-fault circuit interrupter on or near the plug, creating a shock and electrocution risk. The manufacturer has not agreed to a recall.

item.title: Over one million attic stairway ladders recalled over breaking bolts
item.description: Louisville Ladder recalled more than one million Louisville, Featherlite, Lite and Century attic stairway ladders with gas struts because bolts can break. Owners can register for a free repair kit with replacement spreader bolts.

item.title: New Hampshire's home electrification rebates expected to launch in fall 2026
item.description: New Hampshire's Department of Energy says its HEAR program, with rebates of up to $14,000 for heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, wiring and insulation, is expected to launch in fall 2026. Only projects started after launch will qualify.

item.title: Harvard housing researchers project home improvement spending growth slowing through 2026
item.description: The Leading Indicator of Remodeling Activity from Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies projects owner spending on improvements and maintenance growing about 2.1 percent by mid-2026 and easing to 1.6 percent by year end, reaching about $518 billion.
